answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent stakes coins before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers flag bad work. A Sybil swarm must fund every copy, so its cost scales linearly while its payoff stays flat. The honest signal is the stake history — a new identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns standing only through verified work. The delta between a bonded agent and a throwaway identity is what keeps the swarm unprofitable.
